jurisdiction.name: Colombia
jurisdiction.overview: Nationally published records appear separately from applicable EU-level records. The landscape, historical relationships and legal applicability remain under document-level review.

narrative.summary: Colombia governs AI mainly through national policy documents of the National Council for Economic and Social Policy (CONPES): CONPES 3975 of 2019 on digital transformation and AI, and CONPES 4144 of 2025, the dedicated National AI Policy. These are supported by a 2021 ethical framework for AI and a public-sector AI ethics guide, a 2021 presidential directive on AI use in government, and the data protection authority's (SIC) 2024 circular on personal data in AI systems. Binding AI rules include the judiciary's 2024 guidelines on AI use by courts, a 2025 joint directive of the Inspector General and the Ombudsman on algorithmic transparency in the State, and Law 2502 of 2025, which penalises impersonation using AI. A comprehensive risk-based AI bill is pending in Congress.
lead_institutions: Ministry of Information Technologies and Communications (MinTIC)
narrative.review_notes: This review was carried out on 12 October 2026 from documents read in full on official sites. The 2025 National AI Policy is recorded from official records. Not yet verified from the official text: the full text of the 2025 National AI Policy and the status of AI bills in Congress. The pending AI bill is tracked as a lead.

instruments.english_title: Ethical Guide for the Implementation, Development and Use of Artificial Intelligence Systems in Public Entities of Colombia
instruments.issuing_authority: Presidency of the Republic (Office of the High Advisor for Digital Transformation), with the Ministry of ICT, the Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation, the Communications Regulation Commission and the National Planning Department
instruments.publisher_name: Ministry of Information Technologies and Communications
instruments.current_status: Published by MinTIC as an implementation action of CONPES 4144 (news page dated 'Última actualización: 07 de enero de 2026'; the PDF itself carries no date). The guide is addressed to national-level public entities; no adopting act making it mandatory was found.
instruments.summary: 62-page guide for national public entities that sets fundamental ethical principles and values for responsible AI in the Colombian public sector, drawing on the OECD AI Principles, UN guiding principles, the UNESCO Recommendation and the Alan Turing Institute framework. It explains how to put them into practice through enablers, safeguards and good practices (including algorithmic impact assessments, public registers of AI systems and alignment with Joint Directive 007 of 2025 on algorithmic transparency) and includes an illustrative health-sector case study.

instruments.issuing_authority: Administrative Department of the Presidency of the Republic
instruments.publisher_name: Administrative Department of the Presidency of the Republic
instruments.current_status: Edition dated October 2021 (72 pages), prepared by the Presidency with support from CAF and IDB. Followed for public entities by the 2025/2026 Ethical Guide for public entities; not formally withdrawn.
instruments.summary: Presidency framework that sets ethical principles for the design, development and use of AI in Colombia, including transparency and explanation, privacy, human control of decisions, security, responsibility, non-discrimination, inclusion and the prevalence of children's rights. It pairs the principles with implementation tools for public entities (such as algorithm evaluation, risk management for privacy and a follow-up dashboard) and data-ethics guidance on data provenance and processing.

instruments.official_title: Circular Externa No. 002 de 2024: Lineamientos sobre el Tratamiento de Datos personales en Sistemas de Inteligencia Artificial
instruments.english_title: External Circular No. 002 of 2024: Guidelines on the Processing of Personal Data in Artificial Intelligence Systems
instruments.current_status: Issued 21 August 2024 to entities supervised by the SIC in its role as personal data protection authority.
instruments.summary: Data protection authority circular addressed to data controllers, processors, sources, operators and users under Statutory Laws 1581 of 2012 and 1266 of 2008 that develop, deploy or use AI systems. It sets guidelines for processing personal data in AI systems, including a suitability, necessity, reasonableness and strict proportionality test, risk identification and mitigation under demonstrated accountability, a precautionary approach where harms are uncertain, and respect for data subjects' authorisation and purpose limitation.

instruments.official_title: Ley 2502 de 2025, por medio de la cual se modifica y establece un agravante al artículo 296 de la Ley 599 del 2000, Código Penal colombiano y se dictan otras disposiciones
instruments.english_title: Law 2502 of 2025 amending and establishing an aggravating circumstance in article 296 of Law 599 of 2000 (Colombian Criminal Code) and issuing other provisions
instruments.issuing_authority: Congress of the Republic of Colombia
instruments.publisher_name: Ministry of Information Technologies and Communications
instruments.current_status: Enacted 28 July 2025; published in Diario Oficial No. 53.198 of 31 July 2025. Under article 6 the law applies from publication, but the amendment to article 296 of the Criminal Code takes effect one year after sanction and promulgation (from late July 2026).
instruments.summary: Law that adds an aggravating circumstance to the offence of personal falsehood (article 296 of the Criminal Code): when the impersonation is carried out using artificial intelligence the fine increases by up to one third. It defines deepfakes, identity, image and individuality, orders the national government, the Attorney General's Office, the National Police and the Ministry of Justice, with MinTIC, to formulate a public policy on AI used to deceive or cause harm, and requires the Attorney General's Office to track AI impersonation cases and report annually to Congress.

instruments.official_title: Ley Estatutaria 1581 de 2012, por la cual se dictan disposiciones generales para la protección de datos personales
instruments.english_title: Statutory Law 1581 of 2012 issuing general provisions for the protection of personal data
instruments.issuing_authority: Congress of the Republic of Colombia
instruments.publisher_name: Ministry of Information Technologies and Communications
instruments.current_status: Dated 17 October 2012; published in Diario Oficial No. 48.587 of 18 October 2012. General data protection law (no AI-specific provisions); its regime is the basis of SIC External Circular 002 of 2024 on AI.
instruments.summary: Colombia's general data protection statute, which develops the constitutional right (article 15) to know, update and rectify personal information held in databases. It sets the principles for processing personal data (purpose, freedom, accuracy, transparency, restricted access and circulation, security, confidentiality), requires prior authorisation from data subjects, and gives the Superintendence of Industry and Commerce supervisory and sanctioning powers that apply to data used to train and operate AI systems.

instruments.official_title: Acuerdo PCSJA24-12243 de 2024, por el cual se adoptan lineamientos para el uso y aprovechamiento respetuoso, responsable, seguro y ético de la inteligencia artificial en la Rama Judicial
instruments.english_title: Agreement PCSJA24-12243 of 2024 adopting guidelines for the respectful, responsible, safe and ethical use of artificial intelligence in the Judicial Branch
instruments.current_status: Issued 16 December 2024 (session of 11 December 2024); the judiciary's register lists it as 'Vigente sin modificaciones'. It applies from publication (article 16). Adopted following Constitutional Court judgment T-323 of 2024 on judges' use of generative AI.
instruments.summary: Binding guidelines for magistrates, judges and employees of the Judicial Branch on using AI tools, especially general-purpose generative AI, in judicial and administrative work. It sets principles and guarantees, classifies permitted uses, limits other uses of generative AI to tools provided or endorsed by the Council, and requires suitability analysis before use, human control and verification of outputs, and explicit disclosure in the case file of the tool, model, provider, date and prompts used; it also assigns institutional AI projects, training (Escuela Judicial) and monitoring mechanisms.

instruments.official_title: Directiva Conjunta No. 007 de 2025: Estándares sobre transparencia algorítmica para los sistemas algorítmicos utilizados por el Estado
instruments.english_title: Joint Directive No. 007 of 2025: Standards on algorithmic transparency for algorithmic systems used by the State
instruments.issuing_authority: Inspector General of the Nation (Procuraduría General de la Nación) and Ombudsman (Defensoría del Pueblo)
instruments.current_status: Signed 30 September 2025 in compliance with order four of Constitutional Court judgment T-067 of 2025; in force from promulgation, with a six-month compliance period for obligated entities (article 30). Full text also in the MinTIC legal compilation (directiva_procuraduria_0007_2025). The Ministry of Public follow-up table was installed in September 2026 (Ombudsman news).
instruments.summary: Joint directive of the Inspector General and the Ombudsman setting minimum algorithmic transparency standards for all entities obliged under the access-to-information law (Law 1712 of 2014) that develop, acquire or use algorithmic systems involving AI, automated decision-making or sensitive tracking data. It requires proactive publication of information on each system's design, purpose, operation and effects, a channel to object to or seek review of automated decisions, prior algorithmic impact analysis for higher-risk systems, rules for chatbots, access to source code with exceptions, annual reporting and transparency clauses in contract planning.

instruments.official_title: Decálogo de Inteligencia Artificial para la Educación Superior en Colombia
instruments.english_title: Decalogue on Artificial Intelligence for Higher Education in Colombia
instruments.current_status: Document carries '© Ministerio de Educación Nacional de Colombia, 2026' and no precise date; prepared by the Vice-Ministry of Higher Education with the National Higher Education Council (CESU).
instruments.summary: Ten-point ethical and operational orientation from the Ministry of Education for higher education institutions on governing AI, grounded in the six strategic axes of CONPES 4144 and its risk-mitigation lines. It calls for institutional AI governance models with algorithmic transparency and data integrity, preservation of human interaction in teaching, equitable access to close regional gaps and technological sovereignty through local solutions, while respecting institutional autonomy.

instruments.current_status: Nine-page PDF on the Ministry's site, printed '© Ministerio de Educación Nacional de Colombia, 2026'; no month or day is stated. It describes itself as an ethical and operational orientation that respects institutional autonomy; no adopting act was found.
instruments.summary: Ten-point ethical and operational orientation for higher-education institutions on AI, built on the six axes of CONPES 4144 of 2025. It covers ethics and institutional governance (algorithmic transparency, data integrity, multi-level governance models), infrastructure and data, interdisciplinary research, training of staff and students, and inclusion and sustainability. It recommends rather than requires and leaves implementation to each institution.
